mentions.name: bUniProbe
mentions.description: Open-source wireless hardware debugger that connects over Wi-Fi and handles SPI, I2C, UART, CAN and GPIO with built-in level shifting between 3.3V and 5V targets. It hosts its own web server so users can monitor signals, read/write data, and toggle hardware pull-ups from a browser without installing drivers, and includes a waveform viewer and a REST API for automating hardware testing with Python scripts. Hardware and firmware are fully open-source; currently in pre-launch on Crowd Supply.
mentions.problem: Debugging hardware previously required juggling separate USB adapters for SPI, I2C, UART, CAN and GPIO and wiring up external level shifters just to switch between 3.3V and 5V targets.
mentions.source_excerpt: I am working on bUniProbe (https://www.crowdsupply.com/bitmerse/buniprobe), an open-source wireless hardware debugger. I was tired of juggling separate USB adapters for SPI, I2C, UART, CAN and GPIO and wiring up external level shifters just to switch between 3.3V and 5V targets.
